chunks: Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā, from Abī al-Miʿzā, from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, from one of the two of them عليهما السلام, who said:
There is no shortening upon the sailors during their travel, nor upon the muleteers, nor upon the camel-drivers.

key_terms.الْجَمَّالِينَ: camel-drivers; those whose livelihood involves continual travel with camels
key_terms.الْمَلَّاحِينَ: sailors; those whose work involves navigation and ongoing travel by water
key_terms.الْمُكَارِينَ: muleteers or transport-hirers; those engaged in transport as an occupation
key_terms.تَقْصِيرٌ: shortening; performing the reduced form of salat in travel
key_terms.سَفَرِهِمْ: their travel; the state of journeying relevant to prayer rulings

ai.seo_question: Who must perform full salat and not shortened salat during travel in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith states a legal ruling that certain people whose occupation is continual travel do not perform qasr during travel. It identifies sailors, muleteers, and camel-drivers as categories for whom full prayer is required while traveling.
